name: South Africa
sources: GDP $126.0bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series ZAF, 1990 - the same series the rest of this roster sits on (Nigeria's 54.0 in nigeria.json is 54,035,795,388 on it, so the convention is verified against a shipped African file rather than assumed). This is by a wide margin the largest economy in sub-Saharan Africa in 1990: bigger than Nigeria, Zaire, Kenya, Ethiopia, Angola, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Uganda, Senegal, Ghana and Cameroon put together, which come to about $102bn between them. It is also an economy that had gone nowhere for a decade - real GDP per head in 1990 was below its 1974 peak, under sanctions, disinvestment and a debt standstill declared in September 1985.

Population 40.7m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series ZAF, 1990 = 40,746,268. CAVEAT: the census of 7 March 1991 counted 38.1m and was accepted at the time to have badly undercounted Africans in the four nominally independent homelands - Transkei, Bophuthatswana, Venda and Ciskei were enumerated separately as foreign states. The World Bank figure is the reconstructed total for the territory the game draws as South Africa, which is the right one here for exactly that reason.

TFP trend 0.002: the floor of the roster's range, and it is not pessimism. Real GDP fell in 1990 and again in 1991 and 1992 - the longest downswing since the 1930s. Capital was leaving, the gold price was falling in real terms, and the import-substituting industrial base built behind sanctions was uncompetitive the moment the sanctions came off. Set below Poland's 0.01 and far below India's 0.02 because South Africa in 1990 is a rich economy that has stopped growing, not a poor one that is about to start.
Inflation 14.3%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, series ZAF, 1990 = 14.32%. South Africa ran double-digit inflation for the whole of the 1980s and it is the reason the Reserve Bank's rate is where it is.

Interest rate 21%: World Bank FR.INR.LEND, series ZAF, 1990 = 21.0, the prime overdraft rate. The World Bank publishes no policy-rate series for South Africa in 1990; the SARB's own Bank rate sat some three points below prime. The prime figure is entered because it is the sourced one and because it is what borrowers actually paid. Real rate against 14.3% inflation is +6.7 points, and the coupled real-rate check in the loader reads 0.025 - (0.21 - 0.143) = -0.042, comfortably inside the band.

Revenue 23.4% of GDP: World Bank GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS, series ZAF, 1990 = 23.36 (central government revenue excluding grants). Provincial and homeland administrations sat on top of this, so the general-government take was higher; the central figure is entered for comparability with the other roster files, which use the same series.

Military 3.9% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, series ZAF, 1990 = 3.90. The highest share in this region outside the two countries actually fighting civil wars (Angola 17.5%, Ethiopia 9.7%), and about double Egypt's 3.5% - which is what a border war in Angola, a counter-insurgency at home and a covert nuclear programme cost together.

Investment: gross capital formation was 18.2% of GDP (World Bank NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, series ZAF, 1990 = 18.23). The 6.0 / 12.2 split between public and private is APPORTIONED rather than transcribed - the World Bank publishes the total, not the split - and it is set at roughly one third public because Eskom, Iscor, Sasol, Armscor and Transnet were state corporations and were where the capital programme was. The two entries sum to the sourced total; only the division between them is a judgement, and it is stated here rather than hidden.

Debt 39% of GDP: NOT SOURCED IN THIS SESSION and listed as an admitted gap. The World Bank's external-debt series (DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS) has no entry for South Africa in 1990 - it was not a reporting debtor, and after the standstill of 1 September 1985 most of its foreign obligations were inside a rescheduling arrangement rather than on the open market. 0.39 is entered as national-government gross loan debt on the order of the figures reported through the early 1990s, and it is the one number in this file that a reader should treat as a bracket rather than a transcription.

Oil 0.0: South Africa produced no crude. What it had instead was Sasol, converting coal to liquid fuel at a cost only an embargoed state would pay, and a strategic stockpile in disused mine shafts at Ogies. The sim's oil channel is crude production, so the honest entry is zero.

Stability 40 and authoritarianism 0.62: the game opens five weeks before F.W. de Klerk's speech of 2 February 1990 unbanning the ANC, the PAC and the SACP, and nine days before Nelson Mandela walked out of Victor Verster. Authoritarianism is set just above the model's 0.60 electoral ceiling, deliberately and on one fact: the last general election, on 6 September 1989, was for the House of Assembly on a whites-only roll of about 3.2m voters in a country of 36-40m. A government that cannot be removed by the people it governs is not electoral, however real the contest among those who could vote - so South Africa in January 1990 gets pillars rather than a next election, and it is the reform in government.rs that has to move it. Stability 40 is set above Nigeria's 35 and below Yugoslavia's 44: the state itself was intact and solvent, but roughly 4,000 people were killed in political violence in 1990, most of it on the Reef between the ANC and Inkatha from August onward.

Separatism 0.15: the same value as India's, and for a comparable reason - a real fracture line that does not break the state. Two of them here: the four nominally independent homelands, which had to be reabsorbed and where Bophuthatswana's army mutinied in 1994; and the Afrikaner volkstaat demand, which the AWB and later the Freedom Front pressed and which took 2.2% of the vote in 1994. Set above Italy's 0.05 and Poland's 0.05, well below Indonesia's 0.35.

Military strength 16 and nuclear FALSE: strength is set level with Spain's 16 and below Yugoslavia's 20 - the SADF was about 106,000 with conscription, and it was the best-trained and most combat-experienced force on the continent by a distance (Cassinga, Operation Modular, Cuito Cuanavale), but it was small, embargoed since UN Security Council Resolution 418 of 4 November 1977, and flying Mirages it had to rebuild itself. THE NUCLEAR FLAG IS AN ARGUED CALL AND THE MOST DEBATABLE FIGURE IN THIS FILE. South Africa had six assembled gun-type devices and a seventh part-built on 1 January 1990, so on a literal reading the flag should be true. It is set false, and because a review has since called this a hard citable error the reasoning is now set out against the rest of the roster rather than on its own. THE CONVENTION THIS ROSTER USES IS OBSERVABILITY - NOT POSSESSION, AND NOT DECLARATION EITHER: the flag models a deterrent that other governments could see and plan around, because deterring is the only thing it does in the model. israel.json is the file that fixes that reading and is the reason declaration cannot be the test - it sets nuclear TRUE while recording in its own sources that Israel 'has never confirmed it and never will', on the ground that Dimona was planned around by every capital in the region in 1990. South Africa is the opposite case on the same axis: the programme was covert in the strong sense rather than merely undeclared, and it was not admitted until de Klerk told Parliament on 24 March 1993, so no government's conduct in 1990 was shaped by it. Israel true and South Africa false is therefore one rule applied twice, not two separate judgement calls. THE POSSESSION FACTS AND THEIR DATES, RECORDED SO THAT NOBODY THINKS THEY WERE MISSED: six assembled gun-type devices and a seventh part-built on 1 January 1990; de Klerk ordered dismantlement on 26 February 1990, 56 days after the game opens; the last device was destroyed by July 1991; accession to the Non-Proliferation Treaty followed on 10 July 1991; the programme was declared to Parliament on 24 March 1993. On a literal possession reading the flag would be true for the first eighteen months of a thirty-year game and false for the remaining twenty-eight and a half. THE MODEL CANNOT EXPRESS THAT, AND THIS WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: nothing anywhere in the sim ever sets a nuclear flag back to false, so the flag is monotone once set; dyads.rs returns zero war appetite outright against a nuclear power, and war.rs cedes it no territory when it loses. Setting it true would hand the sim a South African deterrent running into the 2020s that the real South Africa gave up in eighteen months - a larger and a longer falsehood than the one it would correct. The flip was also run rather than argued: it moves the_1990_start_is_pinned and golden_hash_of_a_known_run, and it knocks a_dead_nation_holds_no_districts and a_large_nation_is_subjugated_rather_than_swallowed off their pinned seeds, so it is a change to the shipped timeline and not a free one-word correction. If the convention is ever changed to possession it must change for South Africa, Israel, Pakistan and India together, and the model needs a disarmament path before it can be. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 1 were held and are listed below with their citations; 47 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_cmos_submicron, core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, core_pcr, comp_microprocessor, comp_risc_superscalar, comp_relational_database, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, comm_cellular_analogue, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_recombinant_pharma, bio_universal_immunisation, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_cross_sectional_imaging, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.
